messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - embeddings.euw1 high error rate detected. Pager triggered by 5xx spike (>40% over baseline). Incident link: https://incidents.redwood.local/1765432199 

oncall-bot: summary -> affected service: embeddings-worker (euw1). Errors: CUDA OOM / 500s in inference path. Customer impact: some real-time search/semantic features degraded.

Asha Patel: taking driver for now. I'm on call until 17:10 UTC, can hold the bridge for the next 10m.

Jordan Kim: I can own comms (updates + customer notifications). Noted - will prepare status messages.

Asha Patel: quick checks I ran:
```
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=embeddings-worker -o wide
# several pods CrashLoopBackOff / OOMKill
kubectl -n inference logs deployment/embeddings-worker --since=15m | grep -i oom
# RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory while allocating tensor
```

Asha Patel: mitigation options from runbook: scale up replicas, failover to emb-quant-v2 (smaller model), or revert recent config that changed batch_size.

Lee Carter: link to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-euw1.md (see "Immediate mitigation" section). Step 1 = scale, Step 2 = failover, Step 3 = notify customers.

Jordan Kim: COMMUNICATIONS plan: Short status now, follow-up 15m, then 30m if not resolved. Draft status: "We are investigating elevated errors affecting embeddings in eu-west1; mitigation in progress; no data loss expected."
Will ping growth/sales if top-account traffic affected.

Asha Patel: I'm going to try harmless scale up first:
```
kubectl -n inference scale deploy embeddings-worker --replicas=6
```
I'll watch CPU/GPU and pod restarts. If OOM persists, we'll flip to quantized variant.

Michael Chen: I'm joining bridge in ~8m (17:02 UTC) and can take driver if Asha needs a break. Also will prepare fallback deploy manifest.

Asha Patel: noted. DRIVER: Asha Patel (current). COMMS: Jordan Kim.

(oncall-bot): runbook-check: last successful failover tested 2025-11-09, rollback-ok.

Asha Patel: scale issued -> pods are recreating but a few still OOM on init (same stacktrace).

Lee Carter: quick diagnostic - any recent model churn or quantization rollout? I see a config change 45m ago that increased max_batch_size to 4096 for embeddings-worker.euw1. Could explain spike.

Asha Patel: reverting that now to 1024:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/embeddings-worker MAX_BATCH_SIZE=1024
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/embeddings-worker
```

Jordan Kim: Jordan -> prepping customer note: "We identified a config change increasing batch sizes in eu-west1; reverting now and scaling_verified. We'll post next update at +15m." @support-team please stand by for account-specific pings.

Michael Chen: FYI I'm at 17:05 UTC on bridge. If we don't see improvements in 7m, I'll trigger failover to emb-quant-v2:
```
# patch deployment to use quantized image
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/embeddings-worker embeddings-worker=registry.redwood/emb-quant-v2:prod
kubectl -n inference rollout status deploy/embeddings-worker
```

Asha Patel: 17:07 - some pods still OOM but error rate down from 42% -> 18%. Good direction.

Jordan Kim: Update posted to status page and sent to affected accounts list. No escalations from sales yet.

Asha Patel: handoff note - I need to step off at 17:10 UTC for a quick break. Michael, can you take driver at 17:10?

Michael Chen: yes, I'll take driver at 17:10 UTC. COMMS remains Jordan unless you want to swap.

Asha Patel: perfect. Handoff checklist copied to thread:
- DRIVER: Michael Chen (taking @ 17:10 UTC)
- COMMS: Jordan Kim (staying on)
- CURRENT MITIGATIONS: reverted MAX_BATCH_SIZE, scaled replicas, monitoring gpu memory + latency
- NEXT: if errors >10% after 10m -> failover to emb-quant-v2 (Michael to execute)
- RUNBOOK ref: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-euw1.md#immediate-mitigation

Jordan Kim: I'll maintain status cadence. If failover happens, I'll update customers with ETA and degraded perf note.

Lee Carter: Coverage gap note: eu-west1 secondary region autoscaler was in maintenance and cannot accept overflow. If failover needed, plan B is spin up dedicated burst pool (requires infra approval). I've opened an infra ticket: INF-9872.

oncall-bot: reminder: please annotate incident with "handoff" and parties: driver=Michael Chen, comms=Jordan Kim.

Michael Chen: 17:10 - I have driver. Observability: error rate steady ~12%, latency increased 30% on quant-approx path. I'll stand by to failover if it creeps back up.

Asha Patel: thanks all, handing off bridge to Michael. Leaving logs & recent commands in thread. Back in ~20m.

Jordan Kim: copy that. Will send 2nd update at +15m. 

Lee Carter: monitoring panels open. Tagging @infra-team for burst pool readiness.

(oncall-bot): incident updated: owners updated. Incident priority remains P1 until errors <5% and stable for 30m.
